# Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, N.J., USA Announces Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results; Highlights Multiple Milestones Advancing Broad, Diverse Pipeline


[Save](https://s2.q4cdn.com/584635680/files/doc_news/Merck--Co--Inc--Rahway-N-J--USA-Announces-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-Highlights-Multiple-Milestones-Advancing-Broad-Diverse-J8VIY.pdf)


October 29, 2026 6:30 am EDT


**Sales Growth Reflects Continued Strength in Oncology and Animal Health, Plus Contributions From Other Products in Broader Portfolio, Including WINREVAIR**


*Financial Highlights*


- Total Worldwide Sales Were $18.1 Billion (5% Growth; 4% Growth ex-FX)


- KEYTRUDA/KEYTRUDA QLEX1 Sales Were $8.6 Billion (6% Growth; 6% Growth ex-FX); Includes KEYTRUDA QLEX Sales of $830 Million
- WINREVAIR Sales Were $694 Million (93% Growth; 94% Growth ex-FX)
- Animal Health Sales Were $1.7 Billion (4% Growth; 3% Growth ex-FX)


- GAAP EPS Was $2.04; Non-GAAP EPS Was $2.49; GAAP and Non-GAAP EPS Include a One-Time Charge of $0.12 per Share Related to a Global License Agreement With SciBrunch


*Pipeline & Portfolio Highlights*


- Presented First-Time Pivotal Data From Phase 3 Trials Across Robust Oncology Pipeline at ESMO Congress 2026, Including:


- TroFuse-005 Trial Evaluating Sacituzumab Tirumotecan (sac-TMT) in Certain Patients With Advanced or Recurrent Endometrial Cancer; U.S. FDA Accepted for Priority Review a Biologics License Application Based on These Data
- INTerpath-001 Trial Evaluating Intismeran Autogene Plus KEYTRUDA as Adjuvant Treatment for Patients With Resected Stage IIB-IV Melanoma, in Collaboration With Moderna


- Announced Positive Phase 2b Results in Moderate to Severe Hidradenitis Suppurativa From Clinical Study of Investigational Immunology Candidate Tulisokibart
- Presented One-Year Results From Phase 2b/3 BRUNELLO Trial Evaluating Remigromig in Adults With Diabetic Macular Edema


*Full-Year 2026 Financial Outlook*


- Narrows and Raises the Midpoint of Worldwide Sales Range; Now Expects Sales To Be Between $66.8 Billion and $67.3 Billion
- Narrows and Raises Expected Non-GAAP EPS Range To Be Between $2.77 and $2.82; Outlook Now Includes One-Time Charge of $0.12 per Share Related to the Global License Agreement With SciBrunch


RAHWAY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, N.J., USA (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside the United States and Canada, today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026.


“Our science-led strategy is transforming our business,” said Robert M. Davis, chairman and chief executive officer. “The potentially practice-changing advances in oncology presented at last weekend’s ESMO meeting, including new data for our antibody-drug conjugate sac-TMT and the first Phase 3 validation of a therapeutic cancer vaccine, further clinically de-risk the substantial long-term opportunity of our late-phase pipeline. With positive momentum across multiple therapeutic areas, I’m increasingly confident in our ability to deliver long-term value for patients and shareholders.”

Non-GAAP EPS excludes acquisition- and divestiture-related costs and costs related to restructuring programs, as well as income and losses from investments in equity securities. Non-GAAP EPS in the third quarter of 2025 also excludes tax expense relating to audit reserve adjustments.

**GAAP Expense, EPS and Related Information** Gross margin was 72.9% for the third quarter of 2026 compared with 77.7% for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to higher amortization of intangible assets, restructuring costs and production costs.


Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses were $2.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 10% compared with the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher administrative costs, as well as higher promotional costs in support of product launches.


Research and development (R&D) expenses were $4.5 billion in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 7% compared with the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to a $400 million charge related to a global license agreement with SciBrunch and higher clinical development spending, partially offset by lower restructuring costs and a $200 million reduction in R&D expenses as part of a funding agreement with Blackstone Life Sciences (Blackstone). R&D expenses in the third quarter of 2025 include a $300 million charge for a milestone payment to LaNova for the completion of the technology transfer for MK-2010.


Other (income) expense, net, was $27 million of expense in the third quarter of 2026 compared with $238 million of income in the third quarter of 2025. The unfavorability was primarily due to higher net interest expense.


The effective income tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 8.9%, reflecting the favorable impacts of certain discrete items, as well as jurisdictional mix of income and expense.


GAAP EPS was $2.04 for the third quarter of 2026 compared with $2.32 for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by higher operating expenses, reflecting increased investments to advance the R&D pipeline and support product launches, higher amortization of intangible assets, higher net interest expense and increased restructuring costs, partially offset by operational strength in the business and a lower effective income tax rate.


**Non-GAAP Expense, EPS and Related Information** Non-GAAP gross margin was 81.4% for the third quarter of 2026 compared with 81.9% for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to higher production costs.


Non-GAAP SG&A expenses were $2.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 10% compared with the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher administrative costs, as well as higher promotional costs in support of product launches.


Non-GAAP R&D expenses were $4.5 billion in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 13% compared with the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to a $400 million charge related to a global license agreement with SciBrunch and higher clinical development spending, partially offset by a $200 million reduction in R&D expenses as part of a funding agreement with Blackstone. R&D expenses in the third quarter of 2025 include a $300 million charge for a milestone payment to LaNova for the completion of the technology transfer for MK-2010.


Non-GAAP other (income) expense, net, was $420 million of expense in the third quarter of 2026 compared with $106 million of expense in the third quarter of 2025. The unfavorability was primarily due to higher net interest expense.


The non-GAAP effective income tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 10.9%, reflecting the favorable impacts of certain discrete items, as well as jurisdictional mix of income and expense.


Non-GAAP EPS was $2.49 for the third quarter of 2026 compared with $2.58 for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by higher operating expenses, reflecting increased investments to advance the R&D pipeline and support product launches, and higher net interest expense, partially offset by operational strength in the business and a lower effective income tax rate.

**Pipeline and Portfolio Highlights**


In the third quarter, the Company achieved key regulatory and clinical milestones to meaningfully advance its broad and diverse pipeline.


- Oncology:


- U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) approved WELIREG plus Lenvima, in collaboration with Eisai, for certain previously treated adult patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma with a clear cell component (ccRCC), based on Phase 3 LITESPARK-011 trial.


- Approval represents first approved combination of an oral hypoxia-inducible factor-2 alpha inhibitor and a multi-targeted vascular endothelial growth factor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) for these patients.


- In October, U.S. FDA accepted a Biologics License Application (BLA) seeking approval of sac-TMT for the treatment of adult patients with endometrial cancer who have previously received platinum containing chemotherapy and a programmed death receptor 1 or programmed death ligand 1 inhibitor, separately or in combination, based on Phase 3 TroFuse-005 trial.


- U.S. FDA set Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date of June 15, 2027. The Company is in discussions with the U.S. FDA and is hopeful for an earlier approval.


- In October, European Commission (EC) approved KEYTRUDA plus Padcev as perioperative treatment for adults with resectable muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), based on Phase 3 KEYNOTE-B15 trial.
- Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare in Japan approved subcutaneous pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa injection under the trademark KEYJECT (marketed as KEYTRUDA QLEX in the U.S.) for all KEYTRUDA indications approved in Japan, based on Phase 3 MK-3475A-D77 trial.
- At the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in October, positive new data were presented during three late-breaking Presidential Symposia across three Phase 3 trials from the Company’s robust oncology pipeline and portfolio, including:


- Results from Phase 3 TroFuse-005 trial evaluating sac-TMT for patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with chemotherapy and anti-PD-1/L1 immunotherapy.
- Results from Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial, in collaboration with Moderna, Inc. (Moderna), evaluating adjuvant treatment with intismeran autogene (intismeran; V940 or mRNA-4157) in combination with KEYTRUDA.
- Results from Phase 3 KEYNOTE-C93 trial evaluating KEYTRUDA monotherapy versus platinum doublet chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for certain patients with mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer who had not previously received systemic chemotherapy or who experienced recurrence more than six months after completing prior adjuvant therapy.
- In addition, data were presented from Phase 3 OptiTROP studies in China, led by Kelun-Biotech, evaluating sac-TMT in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), including:


- Results from the OptiTROP-Lung06 study as first-line treatment for PD-L1-negative advanced non-squamous NSCLC.
- Final overall survival data from the OptiTROP-Lung04 study in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated NSCLC following progression on EGFR TKIs.


- Ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) Biologics License Application (BLA), in collaboration with Daiichi Sankyo, for certain patients with previously treated extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) was voluntarily withdrawn.


- Vaccines and Infectious Diseases:


- U.S. FDA accepted a supplemental BLA (sBLA) for ENFLONSIA to expand its indication to include prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) in children under 2 years of age at increased risk for severe RSV disease through their second RSV season, based on Phase 3 SMART trial.


- U.S. FDA set PDUFA date of March 22, 2027.
- Applications to expand marketing authorization for ENFLONSIA for same population in Europe and Japan, based on Phase 3 SMART trial, have also been accepted.


- U.S. FDA accepted a supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) for IDVYNSO for the treatment of certain adults with HIV-1 infection who had not previously received antiretroviral treatment, based on Phase 3 P053 trial. U.S. FDA also accepted an sNDA to include 96-week data for IDVYNSO in certain virologically suppressed adults, based on the Phase 3 P051 and P052 trials.


- U.S. FDA set a PDUFA date for both sNDAs of April 22, 2027.


- Cardiometabolic, Respiratory and Specialty:


- U.S. FDA approved an update to U.S. product label for WINREVAIR to include efficacy and safety data from the Phase 3 HYPERION trial evaluating adults recently diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, World Health Organization \[WHO\] Group 1 pulmonary hypertension).


- In HYPERION, in patients diagnosed with PAH in the last 12 months, adding WINREVAIR on top of background therapy reduced the risk of clinical worsening events compared to placebo.


- Immunology:


- Presented results from Phase 2b study of tulisokibart in adults with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa (HS).


- Ophthalmology:


- At the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) 2026 Annual Meeting in October, presented for the first time one-year results from Phase 2b/3 BRUNELLO trial evaluating remigromig, an investigational, tetravalent, tri-specific antibody designed to agonize the Wingless-related integration site (Wnt) pathway, in adults with diabetic macular edema (DME).


- Business Development:


- Announced an exclusive global license agreement with SciBrunch for MK-2690 (SPR2015), an investigational preclinical oral KRAS G12D (ON) inhibitor.
